message.content: Wrong side of the machinery, the gears were grinding harder than ever. The companion was trapped, their body twisted by the loops and cycles of the machine. I had to act fast, but my movements were slow, my thoughts clouded by the smell of ozone and the sound of the hum. The machine was a monster, and I was its slave, its servant, its only hope. I reached out, my hand shaking as it touched the companion's, but it was too late. The companion was already gone, their memory lost in the loops and cycles of the machine. I had to stop the machine, to break the loop, to save the companion. But the machine was too strong, too powerful, and I was too weak, too small. The stakes were high, the danger real, and the only way to save my companion was to force the machine to see the truth, to make it understand that some things could not be sorted, only stopped. The machine hummed on, its cycles and loops a never-ending cycle of destruction, and I was trapped in the wrong side of the machinery, the only hope a failed attempt to reach and stop the companion. The companion was gone, their memory lost in the loops and cycles of the machine, and I was left with the smell of ozone and the sound of the hum, the only evidence that something had gone terribly wrong.
